records.Japanese:
ここまでは大丈夫かのう？
さて、これからは航海士のこと、つまり
わしらのことについて教えよう
records.previous_English: Still with me? Now let me explain the navigators--people like us.
records.english: Still with me? I'll show you what we do as navigators.
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.source_meaning: Julio checks that Rafael is following and introduces the work that he and the other navigators do.
records.context: Julio checks whether Rafael has followed the lesson. He explains how to assign navigators, what each Deck job does and which jobs are enough for ordinary sailing. A system panel then tells Rafael how to open Deck View.
records.localization_note: Keep the familiar question. Let Julio include himself in the lesson in the same sentence and lead naturally into assigning duties.
compiled_lines: Still with me? I'll show you
records.qa_waiver_reason: The question and the spoken lead fill the first line. The description of what navigators do fits on the second.

records.Japanese:
提督の大事な仕事のひとつに
『人事』というものがある
records.previous_English: One of an admiral's main jobs is assigning duties.
records.english: One of an admiral's main jobs is assigning duties.
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.source_meaning: Assigning people their duties is one of an admiral's important jobs.
records.context: Julio checks whether Rafael has followed the lesson. He explains how to assign navigators, what each Deck job does and which jobs are enough for ordinary sailing. A system panel then tells Rafael how to open Deck View.
records.localization_note: Keep the simple statement of the admiral’s responsibility. The next turn shows how to do it.

records.Japanese:
航海を快適に行うために
それぞれ航海士の担当を決める
わけじゃな
実際に甲板を見ながら行うのじゃ
records.previous_English: Give each navigator a job so the voyage goes smoothly. Let's do that in Deck View.
records.english: Give each navigator a job so the voyage goes smoothly. Let's do that in Deck View.
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.source_meaning: To make the voyage go smoothly, give each navigator a duty while looking at the Deck screen.
records.context: Julio checks whether Rafael has followed the lesson. He explains how to assign navigators, what each Deck job does and which jobs are enough for ordinary sailing. A system panel then tells Rafael how to open Deck View.
records.localization_note: Retain the reason for dividing the work and the exact Deck View command that Julio uses to demonstrate it.

records.Japanese:
まず、艦長はFIじゃ
艦長がいないと船はうごかん
勝手にどこかへ行くわけにはいかん
からのう
records.previous_English: First, you're the captain, FI. A ship can't sail without a captain. It can't choose where to go on its own.
records.english: First, you're the captain, FI. A ship can't sail without a captain. It can't choose where to go on its own.
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.source_meaning: Julio says Rafael is the captain. A ship needs a captain and cannot sail off by itself.
records.context: Julio checks whether Rafael has followed the lesson. He explains how to assign navigators, what each Deck job does and which jobs are enough for ordinary sailing. A system panel then tells Rafael how to open Deck View.
records.localization_note: The repetition makes Julio's point conversationally. Preserve all four rows, the normal F and the live name.

records.Japanese:
次は、操帆手じゃな
風に対して帆の角度を調節してくれる
マストの数と同じだけの操帆手が
必要じゃ
records.previous_English: Next is the Sail Handler. They adjust the angle of the sails to the wind. You'll need one for each mast.
records.english: Next is the Sail Handler. They adjust the sails' angle to the wind. Each mast needs one.
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.source_meaning: A Sail Handler adjusts the sails to the wind. Each mast needs one.
records.context: Julio checks whether Rafael has followed the lesson. He explains how to assign navigators, what each Deck job does and which jobs are enough for ordinary sailing. A system panel then tells Rafael how to open Deck View.
records.localization_note: Keep the Sail Handler title, the exact adjustment and the one-per-mast rule. Give the staffing rule a complete clause.
compiled_lines: to the wind. Each mast needs one.
records.qa_waiver_reason: The sail angle and its relation to the wind stay clear. The one-per-mast rule ends the third line as a whole sentence.

records.Japanese:
それから、操舵手じゃ
船を速く回頭させたいなら重要になって
くるぞい
records.previous_English: When you need to turn the ship quickly, the Helmsman is the one to count on.
records.english: To turn the ship quickly, count on your Helmsman.
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.source_meaning: The Helmsman matters when you want the ship to turn quickly.
records.context: Julio checks whether Rafael has followed the lesson. He explains how to assign navigators, what each Deck job does and which jobs are enough for ordinary sailing. A system panel then tells Rafael how to open Deck View.
records.localization_note: Keep the instruction direct and put turning the ship quickly in one phrase. The next turn supplies the battle example.
records.qa_waiver_reason: The first line gives the maneuver. The second keeps Julio’s recommendation together.

records.Japanese:
海戦の時でも、操舵手が優秀じゃと
船を素早く、有利な位置に
持っていくことができるように
なるわけじゃ
records.previous_English: A skilled helmsman can quickly maneuver the ship into a favorable position in battle.
records.english: A skilled helmsman can quickly maneuver the ship into a favorable position in battle.
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.source_meaning: A skilled helmsman can maneuver the ship quickly into an advantageous position during battle.
records.context: Julio checks whether Rafael has followed the lesson. He explains how to assign navigators, what each Deck job does and which jobs are enough for ordinary sailing. A system panel then tells Rafael how to open Deck View.
records.localization_note: The second sentence develops the previous turn with the maneuvering example and its tactical payoff.

records.Japanese:
それから、副官。いなくても船は
動くのじゃが、いれば、他勢力と交渉が
できるし、航海中、みんなが疲れにくく
なる。縁の下の力持ちじゃな
records.previous_English: A First Mate is optional, but lets you negotiate with other powers and keeps the crew from tiring so fast at sea. An unsung hero.
records.english: A First Mate is optional, but lets you negotiate with other powers and keeps the crew from tiring so fast at sea. An unsung hero.
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.source_meaning: A ship can sail without a First Mate, but the job enables talks with other powers and reduces fatigue at sea. Julio calls it important work that goes unnoticed.
records.context: Julio checks whether Rafael has followed the lesson. He explains how to assign navigators, what each Deck job does and which jobs are enough for ordinary sailing. A system panel then tells Rafael how to open Deck View.
records.localization_note: Keep the optional First Mate and both benefits. The separate closing compliment is Julio’s, and the complete explanation still fits one page.

records.Japanese:
測量士がいれば『自動移動』ができたり
艦隊の緯度経度が分かるようになる
けっこう重要な仕事じゃぞい
records.previous_English: With a Surveyor, you can use Auto Move and see the fleet's latitude and longitude. It's an important job.
records.english: With a Surveyor, you can use Auto Move and see the fleet's latitude and longitude. It's an important job.
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.source_meaning: A Surveyor allows automatic movement and gives the fleet's latitude and longitude. It is fairly important.
records.context: Julio checks whether Rafael has followed the lesson. He explains how to assign navigators, what each Deck job does and which jobs are enough for ordinary sailing. A system panel then tells Rafael how to open Deck View.
records.localization_note: Keep Auto Move as the exact command and let the two coordinates stay together. The short final sentence conveys Julio’s judgment of the job.

records.Japanese:
見張りは、洋上で他の船の所属や
街のようすなどを報告するのが仕事じゃ
records.previous_English: At sea, the Lookout tells you who other ships belong to and what's happening in nearby towns.
records.english: At sea, the Lookout tells you who other ships belong to and what's happening in nearby towns.
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.source_meaning: The Lookout reports who other ships belong to at sea and what is happening in towns, among other things.
records.context: Julio checks whether Rafael has followed the lesson. He explains how to assign navigators, what each Deck job does and which jobs are enough for ordinary sailing. A system panel then tells Rafael how to open Deck View.
records.localization_note: Keep the two distinct reports from the Lookout, ship affiliation and town conditions, in Julio’s everyday language.

records.Japanese:
普通に船を出すだけなら
だいたいこれでよいはずじゃ
あとはいろいろ研究してみるとよいぞ
records.previous_English: That's about all you need to set sail. Try out the other jobs and see what they do.
records.english: That's about all you need to set sail. Try out the other jobs and see what they do.
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.source_meaning: Those jobs should be enough for ordinary sailing. Julio recommends trying out the others.
records.context: Julio checks whether Rafael has followed the lesson. He explains how to assign navigators, what each Deck job does and which jobs are enough for ordinary sailing. A system panel then tells Rafael how to open Deck View.
records.localization_note: The cautious “about all” stays, and the invitation to try other jobs leads to the separate system instruction.

records.Japanese:

『甲板画面』を選んでください
甲板画面では、航海士の担当を変更
できます
